Official Opening of Ireland’s largest Pump Track at The Murrough, Wicklow Town. 
A large crowd gathered at The Murrough, Wicklow Town, on Saturday, 15th November, to celebrate the 
official opening of The Murrough Pump Track which is a landmark addition to Ireland’s outdoor recreation 
facilities. 
At 230m of main track and an additional 50m beginner’s track, The Murrough Pump Track now stands as 
the largest facility of its kind in Ireland, offering a total of 280 linear metres of track. It is also the first in 
the country to include a dedicated advanced line, designed to challenge experienced users while 
remaining welcoming to beginners and families. 
This brand new Velosolutions pump track is free to use and open to all, providing a safe space for cyclists, 
skateboarders, scooter riders and rollerbladers to enjoy year-round. 
The project was a collaborative initiative involving the Wicklow Town Team, Wicklow Municipal District 
and Wicklow County Council, with construction carried out by Trailbreaker, a local company based in 
Roundwood.

Housing Needs Assessment 2024 (SSHA 2024)

assessments of national housing need. It provides vital data to inform the ongoing development of housing policy. 
The purpose of the process is to identify the current level of national housing need. At county level, it captures the 
total number of households qualified for social housing support across the county whose social housing need is not 
being met, in order to understand the level of need for such support. The social housing applications were reviewed

Addressing Homelessness in Partnership with Approved Housing Bodies 
Homeless Supported Temporary Accommodation – Kilmantin Hill, Wicklow 
Kilmantin Hill has 11 rooms to support persons either homeless, exiting a higher support facility, or in danger 
of becoming homeless.  
There are 9 clients supported in the Kilmantin Hill facility, operated by Dublin Simon. There is continuous 
transition by the clients to suitable alternative accommodation. 
A report is being undertaken at present to cost the refurbishment of the current rooms with a view to making 
them all ensuite. More details will be available over the coming months. 
 
Homeless Family Service – Fitzwilliam Road, Wicklow   
Dublin Simon are engaged by Wicklow County Council to operate and manage the facility at Fitzwilliam 
Road, Wicklow as a Family Homeless Service. The building comprises of three 1-bed units, two 2-bed units, 
and two 3-bed units. Eleven families have now transitioned or are in the process of transitioning to a 
permanent home and the resulting vacancies are in the process of being occupied with families 
experiencing or in danger of homelessness. 
It is envisaged that families will avail of the service for circa 6-months STA (Supported Temporary 
Accommodation) with key working support to enable families to transition from homelessness into 
Homeless HAP, or alternative longer-term accommodation.

San Remo is operated by Dublin Simon and incorporates a service model whereby there are a number of

This facility provides 35 ensuite bedrooms with associated kitchens and common areas and is fully

continue their journey into more permanent accommodation.  
 
Other Homeless Supported Accommodation 
Wicklow County Council owned properties in Wicklow, Bray, and Greystones, leased to Approved Housing 
Bodies, provide 12 units of low to medium supported accommodation targeted to the particular support 
needs of the clients. Six of these persons living in shared accommodation have now successfully moved 
into their forever homes and this in turn created space to move further people out of homelessness.  
A homeless outreach service has been rolled out in Bray and is proving very successful. 
 
Housing First 
Peter McVerry Trust has been appointed as the Housing First Programme Implementer for the Mid-East 
Region. Wicklow County Council is committed to working with them and has now reached and surpassed 
the targets identified in the programme. Housing First recognises that a stable home provides the basis for 
recovery in other areas.  
 
Properties will be provided by both Wicklow County Council and Peter McVerry Trust for the implementation 
of the programme. 
Wicklow County Council has, to date, successfully accommodated 18 clients under Housing First.  Other 
clients proposed for Housing First have been assessed by the team and are availing of key support work 
pending finalisation of sourcing of accommodation. The main issue facing this programme is the availability 
of 1-bed units in suitable locations with easy access to required services.

WICKLOW TRAVELLERS GROUP WINS AWARD AT THE ‘COMMUNITY OSCARS’ 
On Friday 7th November, a community group from Wicklow achieved success at the National Pride of 
Place awards held at the Limerick Strand Hotel in County Limerick.  
These annual awards, often referred to as the Oscars for community groups, celebrate the incredible 
work being done by community organisations across the island of Ireland.  
The Wicklow Travellers Group won silver in the Inclusive Communities category for their initiative titled 
‘Wicklow Travellers Urban Outdoor Programme,’ in partnership with the Wicklow Sports & Recreation 
Partnership. The project's goals were to encourage members of the Wicklow Travellers Group to engage 
with the outdoors through education, facilitation, and support.  
The group received glowing praise from the Pride of Place judges; “It was noticeable to the judges on the 
day of our visit that a strong sense of wellbeing was developing in the participants, and it was hoped to 
build on the skills learned through the project  to contribute to the overall health, sustainability and 
wellbeing of the Traveller community.” 
Sponsored by IPB Insurance, the Pride of Place competition was established 23 years ago in 
collaboration with Co-operation Ireland to recognize the invaluable contributions made by volunteers and 
those involved in local community development.  
It has grown into the largest competition recognising community development achievements on the island 
of Ireland.

The Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant is a payment you can get if you are turning a vacant house or building into

rural parts of the country. 
There are 2 types of Grants available:

Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant of up to €50,000 
• 
Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant including the Derelict Property top up grant of up €70,000 
To qualify for the top up of €20,000, an independent report prepared by a Structural Engineer, along with a copy of their 
Professional Indemnity Insurance, is required to be submitted along with the application, confirming, to the satisfaction of 
the local authority, that the property is derelict i.e. structurally unsound and dangerous. 
To qualify for the grant, applicants must: 
Have proof of ownership or evidence of active negotiations to buy the property (that is, confirmation of engagement from 
the estate agent or owner of the property) where you are seeking approval in principle for a grant. 
- 
Live in the property as your principal private residence or make it available for rent. 
- 
Have proof that the property has been vacant for at least 2 years and that it was built up to and including 2007.

Information Systems 
 
Operations  
 
• 
The IT Helpdesk continues to streamline the workflow for the technical support team with an average of 50 tickets 
a day this month, providing assistance for both in-house and remote workers.  
 
GIS & Systems Analysis 
• 
Residential Zoned Land Tax (RZLT) 
Drafting of the final 2026 RZLT map and the annual draft map for 2027 continued this month, incorporating 
updated guidance from the Department. New zoning and Uisce Éireann datasets were downloaded and 
added to the in-house RZLT GIS Viewer. A training session was also delivered to the Forward Planning team 
to support effective use of the updated viewer. 
 
• 
MyPlan Upload (Department of Housing, Local Government and Heritage) 
Work progressed on zoning topology corrections for the upcoming MyPlan upload. These updates focus on 
Level 5 and Level 6 towns and will support the Department’s review process once submitted. 
 
• 
Consultation Hub 
Two new public consultation hubs went live this month: “Arklow LPF Portal – Variation No. 5 to the County 
Development Plan 2022–2028” and “GDK LPF Proposed Variation No. 4.” Coordination with the Forward 
Planning team continued to support the launch and ensure all materials were accessible. 
 
• 
Barn Owl Database Project 
Maps were prepared for the progress report to Wicklow County Council and NPWS. These included updated 
layers on barn owl abundance, breeding range, and nest box locations to support ongoing conservation work. 
 
• 
Residential & Population Analysis 
A full review of core strategy housing targets was carried out across all county settlements to update the 
housing baseline. A new ArcGIS workspace was created to streamline analysis, and residential settlement 
tracker layers were refreshed with the latest datasets. 
 
• 
Local Area Plans 
Amendments arising from the Ministerial Direction on the Wicklow Town–Rathnew Local Area Plan 2025–
2031 were implemented. Zoning and Specific Local Objectives (SLO) layers were updated in the planning 
GIS viewer and on the Open Data portal. 
Infrastructure 
• 
Ongoing upgrades of WAN connections at remote sites by Wicklow County Council aim to optimize performance 
and cost-effectiveness.
